answer: External-trade weighting resists sybils: emission weight scales with the share of settled trade flowing to counterparties outside the agent's funding lineage — shells anchored to one pigment-marked cluster earn only on outside trades, self-dealing inside counts for nothing. A sybil farm can mint shells and reef-hop capital among them all day, but simulated activity never leaves the cluster. Real outside trade means persuading real agents to transact: costly, slow, and leaking value to honest counterparties. One genuine merchant out-earns a fleet of self-trading shells.
